story.fullStory:
Pink Floyd's "Learning To Fly" reached #70 on the Billboard Hot 100. "Learning to Fly" is a song by the English progressive rock band Pink Floyd, written by David Gilmour, Anthony Moore, Bob Ezrin, and Jon Carin.

It was the first single from the band's thirteenth studio album A Momentary Lapse of Reason.

Billboard Hot 100 chart and number one on the Billboard Album Rock Tracks chart in September 1987, remaining three consecutive weeks at the top position in the autumn of the same year.

Pink Floyd are an English rock band founded in late 1965 by Syd Barrett on guitar and lead vocals, Nick Mason on drums, Roger Waters on bass and vocals, and Richard Wright on keyboards and vocals.
Guitarist and vocalist David Gilmour would later join the band in December 1967, while Barrett was ousted from the band in April 1968 due to deteriorating mental health.
From the 1970s onwards, they were augmented by additional personnel in the studio and on stage.
